title: Building State of the Art Open Weights Tool Use: The Command R Family: Sandra Kublik
talk_summary: A Cohere product talk on the Command R/R+ open-weights models, focused on RAG, citations, and multi-step tool use. It is mostly model-marketing, but a few mechanisms (fine-grained citations, plan-reflect-adapt multi-step loop, tool-use preamble) are copyable.

takeaways.what_they_do: Model creates a plan from tool descriptions, calls tools, reflects on results, and revises the plan on error (e.g., retries failed API calls with a new plan).
takeaways.evidence_quote: the model is going to create a plan ... once it calls each tool it's going to reflect on the contents and it's going to adapt the initial plan if it's necessary

takeaways.what_they_do: Train/prompt the model to emit claims tied to specific source spans so users can verify provenance, which they claim lowers hallucination.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're spending extra time to make these citations very fine grained and thanks to that you can experience low hallucination

takeaways.what_they_do: A single large reusable prompt/preamble that explains the full tool-use procedure (plan, call, reflect, retry) is applied consistently across the model family.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's a massive prompt that explains the model what it needs to do in order to get the job done

takeaways.technique: Small specialized model for RAG/tool use
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues a smaller model optimized for retrieval/tool use can replace a pipeline of larger LLMs at lower cost.
takeaways.numbers: 3-5x cheaper than GPT-4 Turbo/Claude Opus claimed

takeaways.technique: Explicit separation of retrieved context vs conversation history
takeaways.what_they_do: Prompt the model to distinguish retrieved documents from chat history and to decide when external retrieval is even needed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: know how to differentiate between the conversation history that the model has with the user and the retrieved information
